builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Economic World Model
summary: The framework replaces purely hand-specified structural economic models and direct LLM policy decisions with a hybrid pipeline: household policies learned from microdata, a calibrated structural transition model from macro data, and a simulator an LLM agent queries before acting. It costs a full modelling and calibration effort over proprietary micro and macro datasets, plus an evaluation stack for distributions, forecasts, and counterfactuals; the LLM planning gain is small, simulation-bound, and validated only against a benchmark life-cycle model's short-run transmission. It can fail through distribution shift between training data and deployment conditions, misspecified structural transitions that invalidate counterfactuals, and simulated-GDP gains that do not transfer to real economic outcomes.
rationale: This is a domain-specific economic simulation research framework, not a deployable LLM efficiency or agent technique, so it has no production role for a constrained-infrastructure practitioner outside economic policy modelling.
technique: Learned economic world model for LLM planning

claims.statement: The framework replaces purely hand-specified structural economic models and direct LLM policy decisions with a hybrid pipeline: household policies learned from microdata, a calibrated structural transition model from macro data, and a simulator an LLM agent queries before acting. It costs a full modelling and calibration effort over proprietary micro and macro datasets, plus an evaluation stack for distributions, forecasts, and counterfactuals; the LLM planning gain is small, simulation-bound, and validated only against a benchmark life-cycle model's short-run transmission. It can fail through distribution shift between training data and deployment conditions, misspecified structural transitions that invalidate counterfactuals, and simulated-GDP gains that do not transfer to real economic outcomes.

Simulated household consumption distributions overlap observed microdata by 94.9%; an LLM agent using the EWM for ex ante planning achieves 10.29% higher simulated GDP under an epidemic shock than direct LLM decisions (reported in simulation only).
